For σ ∈ Sn and τ ∈ Sm , where n ⩽ m, let
           dflex
            n (σ, τ ) = (1/n) · (|{x ∈ {1, . . . , n} | σ(x) ̸= τ (x)}| + (m − n)).
An almost-homomorphism {fn } is said to be flexibly close to a homomorphism if
there is a sequence of group homomorphisms ρn : G → Smn with n ⩽ mn such
that dflex
        n (ρn (g), fn (g)) → 0 as n → ∞ for all g ∈ G. The group G is said to be
flexibly permutation stable if every almost-homomorphism of G is flexibly close to
a homomorphism.
    Is SLn (Z) flexibly permutation-stable?                                      A. Lubotzky
